utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are present. And presentation is exactly like yesterday except that instead of Mr. Thayer we now have the pleasure of the presence of Mr. McCloskey. Good morning to you, general and welcome once more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to continue with your testimony. Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While he is being shown these document, there are three very short oral decisions that would like to give, because otherwise, I'll forget. On the 11th of November, the Nikolic Defence team, filed a confidential motion inviting the Trial Chamber to exercise its discretionary powers pursuant to Rule 98 to call a witness. This was joined by the Popovic Defence, and there was a response on behalf of Gvero filed on the 24th of November. And the next -- the following day we had the Prosecution filing a confidential response and corrigendum. On the 2nd December the Nikolic Defence filed a confidential motion seeking leave to reply and also containing a reply to the Prosecution for the responses. Purpose of this intervention this morning on our part is to inform you that the Trial Chamber will not be responding to the invitation of the Nikolic Defence team. On the 9th of December General Miletic filed a motion seeking leave to add a document to the Exhibit list and have it admitted in evidence. And it's response of the 23rd December, the Prosecution did not object. For all intents and purposes at this stage based on the arguments set forth in the motion, the Trial Chamber grants same. Last on the same day, 9th of December, the Popovic Defence team filed a request for guidelines concerning disclosure of documents obtained during the Defence investigations. On the 17th and 18th of December, Gvero Defence team and Prosecution filed their respective responses respectively. Given the hypothetical nature of the motion, the Trial Chamber hereby dismisses it. Yes, Madam Fauveau sorry for that abrupt interruption, let's proceed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, this is a work-plan of the Skelani command work-plan for February 1995, and you can see that one of the major tasks of the Skelani Battalion in 1995 was to take part in the closing of the frontline in Srebrenica. On the basis of which element did the command of the Skelani Battalion elaborate its plan for February 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every unit of battalion rank and higher up battalion regiments, brigades, corps and the Main Staff of the Army Republika Srpska, according to the valid documents, worked out work-plans, annual work-plans, and based on that monthly work-plans. The Skelani Battalion in the Drina division had as the basis for their work-plan the documents of their superior command and the documents pertaining to the implementation of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who in the commando unit is in charge of elaborating the work-plan of the command?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the battalion commands, the work-plans were elaborated by the deputy commanders. In the commands of regiments, brigades and higher up, it was the chiefs of staff who were responsible for the work-plans, and the assistant of the Chief of Staff for operations and training were in charge of working out those plans.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On the basis of which elements were the officers in charge of operation and activities elaborated these plans?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I just wondered if we could be clear on which level of command we are talking about so that the witness could respond effectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, can you deal with that, Ms. Fauveau, please. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is the work-plan of the Main Staff. Here we have the work-plan of the battalion of Skelani, on the basis of which element did the officers in charge -- in charge of education and operation, could they make annual work-plans?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the work-plans in all the units enumerated were elaborated according to the same methodology, but now I will use only the term the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, it's monthly work-plan was elaborated based on the annual work-plan which had been adopted and verified. Apart from the excerpt from the annual work-plan, all the assistant commanders delivered their proposals for the introduction of new elements into the work-plan. Also the work-plan also included elements obtained from outside and delivered in good time, such as proposals, requests, and so on from the Supreme Command, from the ministry, and in a specific situation, if UNPROFOR delivered some information on time, this would be included in the work-plan for the following month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wonder if my colleague could have the witness clarify what he means by "elaborated." The question related to make work-plan and I don't know that elaborated responds to that, whether it means make or complete or develop. I just wonder if we could clarify this so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain what the Prosecutor has requested, what is meant by plans elaborated on the basis of annual plans? Can you explain what you mean by "elaborate" or "develop"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To elaborate a work-plan means based on the complete proposals that had been processed in view of their contents, these had to be put in order according to the structure, the elements of combat readiness. They had to be harmonised with the participants, all the participants had to be familiar with those elements. They had to be harmonised in relation to time, hours, and those responsible for implementing the individual elements of the plan, and all -- and harmonised with all those who were involved in that work-plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D990, the work-plan of the Drina Corps for February 1995. Would it be possible to see page 2 in B/C/S and page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This number 5, we always have this problem about the enclaves, but at item 10 - this is what I'm interested in - we may see that the Drina Corps was to receive documents from the Main Staff and was to create then the combat documents, make the combat documents. What does this specific task refer to, can you explain?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that this is a work-plan for February, and also bearing in mind that it says here that the task can be received from the 1st to the 28th of February, which means that any day in the month is the day it's expected to arrive, two things can be assumed. The first task which will arrive and which is expected and in the army everybody knows it's always coming, those are the tasks based on the briefing on combat readiness completed in the previous month. And from these tasks and based on the briefing by the supreme commander, other specific tasks may also be expected. In any case, the command here decided that they should be prepared to receive that task and act on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] could the witness be shown now 5D970. This is an order of the 7th February 1995 of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please look at the first part, the preamble, and tell us what it's about, what is this order linked or connected to? What is it about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order issued by the command of the Drina Corps was drafted based on the order by the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska dated the 5th of February 1995, and it is a consequence of the tasks and obligations mentioned at the briefing of the previous month. After every action, inspection, briefing and so on, all the armies stemming from the former JNA expected orders to take measures in order to remove weaknesses and to improve combat readiness, and you can see that the command of the Drina Corps expected this order from the Main Staff and that within a day or two because on the 5th of February, this was done in the Main Staff, they might have received it on the 6th, and within a day or two they had already prepared their own order to be forwarded to the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 2, both for B/C/S and French.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 1.8. Since we have seen a similar task assigned in November 1994 for the Drina Corps, does this task also come from the analysis of the combat readiness done in January 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The source of the task in point 1.8 under the element command is from 1993, and it's a consequence of the fact that the corps command did not carry out that task. I have hardly seen any documents within the past year or year and a half here similar to this one which does not mention this task. That means that this task was not carried out or was not carried out fully, so it was always reiterated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly -- no, now I would like to see 5D969, an order of the 5 February 1995 of the Main Staff to which this order of the Drina Corps refers. May I give the witness a hard copy so that he can see the whole text of the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this: Please look at this order of the Main Staff and tell us whether somewhere in this text a task concerning the enclaves is at all mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, or rather, this order issued by the Main Staff is something I've analysed more than once now and one can see that the enclaves in this order are mentioned only in point 5 [as interpreted] only where the problem of helicopters flying over by night is mentioned bringing in aid without any control which includes weapons and equipment being brought to these two enclaves. According to the order issued by the command of the Drina Corps where sometimes they use the term "separation" and sometimes "closing," such a task did not exist in this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The order of the Drina Corps which we've just seen before this one refers to this order of the Main Staff, doesn't it? Is it -- how is it possible that the tasks given to the corps, the Drina Corps, do not exactly correspond to the task which the Main Staff has entrusted to it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that the order of the Drina Corps does not correspond to the task which the Main Staff has entrusted to it. Analysing the order issue by the Drina Corps and analysing the order issued by the Main Staff on the 5th of February, one can conclude that everything that the Main Staff ordered was included by the command of the Drina Corps in its order. It took the opportunity, and this is not against the rules, to include in the order some things it had omitted to do, and felt it was necessary to reiterate in its order to its subordinate tasks, and this includes the order on the separation of the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau, take it that line 18 previous page, page 7, "point 5" should read "point 15"; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you found it, Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, on page 4, it should be task 15. That's correct. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could the witness be shown P5.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: For the moment the only thing I'm interested in is what can be seen in English, it would be page 2, what can be seen at the top of this first page. It says "very urgent." In the military practice, what does this mean?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military practice when it says "very urgent," that means that the document, once received, must immediately, as soon as possible, be acted upon, but it was always stressed that certain rules and procedures had to be followed. Very urgent means that whatever has to be done should be done as soon as possible while strictly adhering to certain rules and procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One sees on the directive that it bears the date 8th of March, 1995, in light of that date and of the other elements you were able to find in other documents, could you make conclusions about this directive that it was forwarded to the president for signature?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a lot of elements leading to the conclusion that it was given to the president for signature, but then it was given in a rather specific way. A specific way of giving documents for signature means that the draft of that directive was made by the staff of the VRS and that it was sent to the president for signing on a CD or any other medium. By the look of it, this is one of the rare directives that had been made on a computer, mainly documents that I had an opportunity to see were typed on electrical typewriters.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, in fact, my question was about the date at which the document was forwarded. Could you draw a conclusion about the date at which the directive was forwarded to the president for signature?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the date on the directive, it could not have been forwarded to the president for signing after the 8th of March. According to the military practice, it could have been forwarded only on the 7th of March at the latest in order to reserve the number. According to the practice it could not have been forwarded either earlier or later.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be shown Exhibit 5D1322. This is the diary of the secretary of the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic. I would like to have page 29 in B/C/S, and 27 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On this page you see an entry from 7th of March, 1995. At 1400 President Karadzic, according to this diary at any rate, had a meeting with a General Djukic and Minister Nikolic. In light of the fact that the directive is an act which is under state secret -- now, in light of the fact that the directive is a document which falls under state secrecy, General Djukic, the assistant of the commander for logistics, could he have taken the directive to the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could have done that. This method of transferring documents of high top secret nature was in place, but it could have been delivered in a different way as well, in accordance with the regulations that classify this document as a state secret.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And right at the end of that entry, the 7th of March, in English this is on the following page, throughout the whole page you can see that President Karadzic should have called General Mladic. In light of the type of organisation of the Army of Republika Srpska and of that of the Supreme Command, and in light of the working method about the directive, could the President Karadzic have called General Mladic prior to the directive being signed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In normal circumstances when the Main Staff of the VRS had prepared the draft document, and this document needs to be approved and endorsed by the supreme commander, then the draft is reported to the supreme commander by the commander of the army of the VRS. We see here that the word "call" is mentioned, which means called by telephone, so it is highly likely that this directive was sent and that it was said on the phone that it had been sent and that if anything further is needed, then the commander of the VRS was prepared to provide additional explanations.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D975. At 971 rather.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the letter through which the Main Staff transferred the Directive number 7 to the corps. We know that the directive is dated 8th of March, 1995. How do you explain that it was only transferred on the 17th of March in light of the fact that it was a very urgent document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that the directive bears the notice "very urgent" and that the date is the 8th of March, this covering letter with which it was forwarded to the Drina Corps also bear the notice "very urgent," but the date is the 17th of March. The conclusion is that it is very likely that between the 8th and the 17th of March, this directive was being kept by the president or rather the commander in chief of the VRS. It was received either immediately before it was dispatched further, either on the same day or the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1326.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is in fact a very similar letter that is sent to the Herzegovina Corps. You can see that this document was also forwarded on the 17th of March. And before asking you the question, I'd like for you to see 5D1327, which is practically the same document sent to the Sarajevo Corps. So one can see on all of these documents the date 17th of March, 1995. Can you tell us when a document is very urgent, what is the usual time lag for which to be forwarded to the subordinated units once it has been signed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If my colleague would be so kind as to refer to the specific type of document she's talking about in terms of the time lag when it's an urgent document. A directive is obviously different than an order which is different than an instruction, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, a document such as directive, what would be the normal time-frame in which it is to be transferred to the subordinated units after it has been signed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no dead-line of an hour or a day or two for this type of documents. These kind of documents require to be classified as secret to be copied in several copies, and to delivered in a secure manner to units and to be received in the units in a special way. You can notice here in this covering letter sent to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps that they didn't leave anything to chance and that they responded in a proper and appropriate way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now come back to the diary of the President Karadzic's secretary. This is Exhibit 5D1322. And I'd like to have page 33 in B/C/S and 32 in English, please. No, it's actually rather page 31 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, the date shown on the entry I'm interested in is 16th of May, 1996. 16th of May, clearly it's a mistake if you look at the exhibit in its entirety. On that day President Karadzic had a meeting with the General Milovanovic, General Tolimir, and General Subotic. And according to this diary, the meeting went from 1105 up until 1505. In other words it lasted four hours. Now, given the date and the duration of that meeting, and in light of the fact that the directive was forwarded to the corps on 17th of March, 1995, were you able to draw some conclusions from that meeting due to the fact that the meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having carefully analysed all the dates that appear here, and the participants mentioned here, and the order in which they appear, you can arrive at a full picture at how it -- the work was done on Directive number 7. It is known that the idea came up on the 31st of January that probably on the 7th of January it was taken to the supreme commander by a very responsible high ranking officer which supreme commanders appreciate. It is also known that on the 7th of March, a meeting was held with -- and I didn't have this information before but it is known that this meeting took place on the 16th of March which lasted full four hours, and that very important generals attending this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just don't see how this answer isn't completely speculative in light of the fact that the witness has not commented on any minutes concerning these meetings or anything concerning the content of what occurred or as is recorded in the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but he starts his answer with having carefully analysed all the dates that appear here and the participants mentioned here and the order in which they appear. In other words, he himself has provided himself a sort of a basis on which he then moves ahead with his conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour, but I think what he's described is a coincidence among the dates and beyond that we don't have anything of substance concerning the content of the discussions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't go that far as a member of the bench, obviously. Let's leave it and we'll proceed with your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I think that it is very important and one can -- may speculate one way or another, you know, this is an expert witness and not an expert of facts and I think that he is entitled to say how he has reached some conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't denied you or him that. In fact, you should interpret our conclusive intervention to mean let's proceed, leave things as they are and proceed. We are not saying Mr. Vanderpuye was right. Eventually we will decide ourselves what weight to give to the statement of the accused -- of the witness, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, you have already answered this question, but I should like to go further in the detail of this. Before signing the directive which is a military deed, did -- would President Karadzic have consulted with the members of the Main Staff, particularly if he wanted to bring in modifications?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This directive is not a military document, it's a state document issued by the Commander-in-Chief addressed to the military or the Army of Republika Srpska. Only when a document is prepared by the Army of Republika Srpska, then it becomes a military document, and from day one I tried to point at a problem that many people here will understand. When it comes to issuing state orders to soldiers and coordinating them with military orders, it was also discussed by General Wesley Clark in his book. So if -- when a Commander-in-Chief issues a document, he has a need and an obligation to talk to the military in order to avoid issuing directions or tasks that are impossible for the military to carry out. And when I was interrupted earlier, I was speaking about jurisdiction and responsibility. I'm not talking about personalities. I am talking about officers and their responsibilities. The people who are involved in this show that all areas necessary for drafting this kind of document were covered.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now show you Exhibit 5D977.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the document about the forwarding of Directive 7/1. In this document one can see that Directive 7/1 dates from 31st of March, 1995, and you see also that this covering letter is also dated 31st of March, 1995. Now, is this a usual way of transferring a document, i.e., that a document be transferred on the same day?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Directive 7/1 generated from the command, it was approved and signed by the commander at the commander headquarters and was forwarded on the same day. If we make a comparison with Directive 7 where it generated and where it was delivered, I can say that both these directives satisfy these criteria.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: About the Directive number 7, we know that this is a directive from the president of the republic. The person who signs a document, could that person bring in modifications to the drafter which is submitted to them for signature?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the document is signed, then the signatory takes responsibility for it. That implies his right either to deviate completely from the proposal, or to accept it 100 percent, or to accept it to the extent that he believes it to be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now show you two exhibits, the draft order and then the order being signed. First I'd like 5D1342.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the draft order from the president of the republic dated 16th of June, 1995, and I'd like to ask leave to give to the witness the two exhibits, this one and the following one, 5D1341, for him to be able to compare. Now, on the screen I'd like to have page 2, please. Actually, it will be page 3 in English and in B/C/S as well. The end of page 3, the bottom of it. The end of page 3. [In English] It's the same order, just one is signed, the other is not signed. [Interpretation] Now this, I think, is Exhibit 1341. But, you know, I just want to be sure that we have matching numbers, the right numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Okay. So here you see this is Exhibit -- make sure that it matches e-court, this is Exhibit 5D1341. And you can see that the document which was signed by the president of the republic. May we have page 1 of this document, please. Throughout this whole page, you see that this is an order number 01-1118/95 from 16th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show to the witness Exhibit 5D1342, which is the same order but not signed. And here you see the date 16th of June, 1995, number 01-1118/95. And I'd like to show page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: On this page 2, you can see the handwritten changes. Now, if these changes were made by order of President Karadzic, would -- did these modifications have to be incorporated in the final text?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, that's how it should be. There is a methodology used when drawing up documents as important as this one at all levels of command, and even at all levels of management in civilian life. When the final version of a document which is to be signed is adopted, a version of the text is always also adopted including corrections so that the signatory can check whether all the corrections he asked to be made have actually been made.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, in the Army of Republika Srpska, could anyone have changed the text of the directive after the president of the republic has signed it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never come across that level of crime. In a normal situation, it would not occur to anyone to alter anything after a document had been signed. Even if you notice a grammatical error, it must not be changed or corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what were the powers of Colonel Miletic when Directive number 7 was forwarded to the Main Staff signed by the president, bearing the president's signature?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question is how the directive arrived in the Main Staff. Based on the cover letter sent to the commands of the corps or the accompanying document sent to the commands of the corps signed by the Chief of Staff, whoever compiled this accompanying document, it can probably be concluded that forwarding the directive, entering it into the books, and then forwarding it on is something in which General Miletic was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, as a general rule, what could have General Miletic do when he saw the directive if he may have considered that parts of the directive were not compliant with the law of war?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Miletic was duty-bound if he saw that to bring it to the attention of his superior officer, and his superior officer, General Milovanovic, was duty-bound to assess whether General Miletic's warning was justified, and then to alert the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And who was under the obligation of warning President Karadzic that the directive may have included some elements which could have been qualified as being contrary to the law of war?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on Directive 7 through 1, one can see that the command studied Directive 7 and the command of the Army of Republika Srpska at that point was duty-bound to warn the president of Republika Srpska that the directive contains elements not in compliance with the customs of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is only a minor point, Your Honour, at the beginning of his answer he says -- in the transcript it reads Directive 7 through 1, and I believe that, just so if we could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Right. Yes, Ms. Fauveau, I think you can clarify it with the witness. It doesn't make sense as it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what directive you were talking about when you said that the command considered Directive 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I tried to be precise, I have the impression whenever I try to be precise that it raises a problem. I said that the command of the Army of Republika Srpska studied Directive number 7. The conclusion that it studied Directive number 7, I don't have the work-plan, is something I made based on the fact that based on Directive number 7 they compiled Directive 7/1. When they studied Directive 7, the commander of Republika Srpska was duty-bound to alert the commander in chief that Directive 7 contains elements not in compliance with the customs of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, generally speaking if General Miletic as the head of the body in charge of operations and education received an order to prepare or to forward an order with which he did not agree, what were his powers, or rather, what were the possibilities offered to him? What could he do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I didn't understand your question properly. Could you repeat it, please, to avoid problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, if -- when General Miletic did not agree as the head of administration in charge of operational affairs and training, so if he did not agree with a given order that he was supposed to forward or carry out, what were the possibilities offered to him? Is there a way that he could do anything about it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure to be followed by an officer when he sees that an order or a document is not in compliance with the customs of war is prescribed in detail. It implies, one, that he should immediately inform his superior of this. If he sees that his superior is not taking any action, then, two, he is to inform the highest superior. In the particular case of General Miletic, he was duty-bound to inform General Milovanovic of this. If he saw that General Milovanovic is not willing or interested in alerting his superior, then he was duty-bound to inform the commander. He, furthermore, is not duty-bound to act on the document, which in his view is not in compliance with the customs of war, because doing so would constitute a crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Very well. But what were his powers if this is not a crime, but if he is just not in agreement with the order? What were his options?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, he can express his disagreement, but nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you Exhibit 5D1016. This is a document from the Main Staff dated 17th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In this specific case, what was, according to this document, the position of President Miletic [as interpreted] as compared to that of the commander?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a typical example of professionalism. A textbook example. From this document you can see that General Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps, was asking the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska to change his decision in some elements, and this has to do with this reinforcement. And you can see that General Zivanovic asked the same of General Miletic. Although this was not within the purview of General Miletic, he proposed to the commander to inform General Zivanovic, the commander refused. General Miletic, highly professionally, at that time he was a colonel, forwarded the document to the commander of the Drina Corps saying that the commander insisted that the order be carried out in spite of the fact that he is familiar with the standpoint of General Zivanovic and that he advocated that this attitude -- this standpoint be respected. So this is highly professional.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be shown P5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Kosovac, was this sent out on -- in the name of Colonel Miletic, in the name of Main Staff? In what capacity did he send this memo, this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Miletic sent this information to the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska saying that he abides by his standpoint, with a copy to General Zivanovic. So Colonel Miletic by this document conveys the standpoint of the army -- commander of the Army of Republika Srpska to the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not a personal letter, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is a notice that a commanding officer is duty-bound to convey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he added his personal opinion as to the matter? To a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private, no, but personal, yes. So he as the chief for operations and training agreed with the commander. He told the commander of the Drina Corps that he shared that opinion but that his opinion which he had forwarded to his superior had not been adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just one question, if I may, to clarify a point about that exhibit. How can you see that this is an official document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Private documents are not entered in the protocol log-books, especially a strictly confidential document which has a number which refers to previous correspondence and in which highly important matters are mentioned, that is reinforcements consisting of a certain number of men.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be shown Exhibit P5. This is a Directive number 7. And I'd like to give the text of the directive to the witness in its entirety as I think that it will be easier for him to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yesterday we were talking about the method by which decisions are made. What part of this directive is the decision per se?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision here is contained in point 6.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Point 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to all the regulations, it is the fourth element of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this point 4 is on page 8, but before we refer to point 4, I'd like to focus on point 3 which is on page 7 in English and page 11 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please explain the meaning of point 3 in this directive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 3 represents the task of the Army of Republika Srpska. This task implies the following: Every aim that is to be achieved, the forces, the means, the time, and the place have to be specified. And this is provided for the Army of Republika Srpska in point 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who could ascertain or determine point 3 of this directive, the very content of it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task in point 3 is a task emanating from the superior command, and it is defined by the supreme commander. In lieu of the fact that the supreme commander is a civilian, it's logical that when formulating the task, he used a draft and he talked to competent officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At this point one sees the reference to the order of the Main Staff dated 5th of February, 1995. How do you explain the fact that the directive of the supreme commander refers to this order of the Main Staff? This reference is shown in the first paragraph of point 3.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Commander-in-Chief of the Army of Republika Srpska was present when an analysis of combat readiness was made. He spoke at that analysis meeting, provided guide-lines, and all the conclusions that were made were made in compliance with his standpoints. It can clearly be seen here that this stems from the analysis of combat readiness and that that's where the whole idea came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Let's now move to point 4 which is on page 8 in the English version and which is on the screen in the B/C/S version. In your report, and here this is paragraph 125 - but I don't think that it's necessary to show it on the screen - you have analysed this decision. According to this decision, what were the main tasks of the Army of Republika Srpska in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks of the Army of Republika Srpska, the tasks of the Supreme Command, the decision of the Commander-in-Chief mentioned in point 4 was to be later implemented in the tasks issued to the subordinate units. The decision of the Commander-in-Chief is in line with all the standpoints adopted up to that point, and in spite of the fact that its contained in some 10 or 15 lines, it can be reduced to five points. A decisive defence, resolute defence, persistent defence, strengthening the defence line, inflicting losses on the enemy to the greatest possible extent, preventing further break-throughs, and cutting up the territory. These are the decisions that follow from this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We can see in this point 4 that one to two operations at strategic level are mentioned, as well as three or four operations at operational level. And for the transcript in the English version of the directive, there is a mistake because the text in English talks about operations at tactical level, when in fact the original in B/C/S talks about operations at operational level. Yesterday we were talking about levels of command. Could you please tell us the differences between operations at strategic level, and that at operational level?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This difference can be better understood when one analyses the document, which is what I will now proceed to do from that aspect. At the strategic level, a large number of strategic forces have to be involved in a strategic operation. It's led by the staff of the Supreme Command, and at the operative level it's the operative commands that are in charge. So in addition to the level of command, the differences in the aims to be achieved, the forces engaged in those operations, and very often there's a difference in that time in which the operation has to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, in this directive, are the tasks which were entrusted to the Army of Republika Srpska in point 3, were they supposed to be in agreement with the decision?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Harmony between the decision and the task is a prerequisite for the successful implementation of the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in these specific documents, do points 3 and point 4 match?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam. We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. About the directive, I would like now to speak of the tasks of the units, and this is on page 8 of the English, and page 13 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who had the power and the authority to determine the tasks entrusted to the units?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Commander-in-Chief who issued tasks to the units, to the subordinate units, the orders are issued by the commander of the VRS. In this particular instance, the Commander-in-Chief had gone a step forward and issued tasks to subordinate units, which is not contrary to the rules, but it is rather peculiar.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: During the drafting of this document, Directive 7, did the corps commander have the right to make proposals concerning their respective units?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see in the available documentation, and after reading transcripts of General Milovanovic, the VRS adhered to the standard to involve commanders of the corps as much as possible in the decision-making process whenever the possibilities allowed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the task entrusted to the Drina Corps which is described on page 10 in English and 15 in B/C/S. You? The tasks of the Drina Corps as defined in this item number 5, does this tally with the decision made and which is described in item 4.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the key elements for the analysis of this document. I mentioned this several times so far, that a decision sets out when, what, how, and why, and the ultimate goal being to achieve and carry out a task. This example shows that the tasks entrusted to the Drina Corps is not consistent with the decision, that is to say that it contains some elements that are not at all mentioned in the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you tell us what are these elements of the Drina Corps which are not mentioned in the decision?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first passage on the tasks of the Drina Corps is consistent with the part of the decision which speaks about the decisive defence. However, the latter part of this paragraph, actually, the last sentence has no connection whatsoever with this task of putting up decisive defence, nor does it stipulate that the Drina Corps has any possibility to carry out the task in this way. As I put it in my report, this is a typical example of a task that the military is incapable of carrying out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you explain why you consider that this task cannot be done by the army?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to remind you of the year 1995, mid-1995, and the decision taken -- actually, the assessment of the international community that that was the year in which the VRS became inferior in every aspect. That was exactly and precisely the moment that this document speaks about, and that is the moment when the VRS had lost territories in all fronts when offensive battles were being fought with the BH Army, the Croatian Defence Council, and the Croatian army. And if somebody at that point takes a decision for the army to carry out certain operations that would send a message to the civilian population, can only be described as a senseless decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You also wrote in paragraph 139 that this part of the task was illogical. Could you explain why you consider this task as illogical? Is there anything else than what you have just said now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it illogical because it is assigned to the army. It is also illogical for the army to do something contrary to its goal. One of the main objectives sets out in January 1995, and which is contained in every single decision of the Main Staff, and I think that you all notice the phrase to "settle down the front," in other words, to not mount operations, to not make any movement, do not create any problems, and why that was left in. This activity that is required to be carried out here is something completely contrary, i.e., to create problems and to solve them in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 19 in B/C/S, and 14 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Item 6 speaks of combat support. What is the role of the administration in charge of operational and educational matters and matters for support in combat?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no role in providing support to operations. In the preparation of this document, its role is to take over parts of this document from other participants and make it a whole. Let me just remind you that the support of combat operation is a very complex task made up of nine elements which each of them constitute a separate entity.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this item, I see that UNPROFOR is mentioned. Did the cooperation with UNPROFOR in general, the relations with UNPROFOR, and the humanitarian organisations, were they within the purview of the organ in charge of operational and educational matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cooperation with UNPROFOR is a separate activity which is precisely defined in the VRS, and it was under the jurisdiction of the commanders of the Chief of Staff, and if army were to address this issue, it would have done it completely differently. As far as the operations and training administration, had no responsibility and jurisdiction in terms of cooperation with UNPROFOR, and in support of this view, I would like to remind you of the yesterday's conversation between General Nicolai and General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We know that General Miletic signed a certain number of documents which concerns supplies of the UNPROFOR units. This sort of document, does it enable us to conclude that matters linked with UNPROFOR enters within its purview?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no foundation for such a conclusion. The fact that a large number of documents and information bulletins were assigned by a man at the basic command post that could have been forwarded to everybody else could lead to a wrong conclusion. The fact that he signed certain documents does not imply that he had any rights or powers in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The treatment of war prisoners, was it within the competencies of the administration in charge of operational and educational matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Under no circumstances. The staff and the operations and training administration within the staff have no jurisdiction over prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Does the treatment of the civilian population as well Serbian civilian population or other nationalities, does that belong to the competencies of the Administration in Charge of Operational and Educational Matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that on the first day I have highlighted a crucial difference and now is a good time to repeat it. The VRS, the JNA, and all the other armies that emerged from the ex-JNA, as well as the army of the FRY, had no organs or jurisdictions over the treatment of any segment of the civilian population. And by virtue of that this particularly refers to the operations and training administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You already said that this directive was sent to the corps and that it was unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 5D1167.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is a document from the Main Staff which transmits the order of the president of the republic. I would like you to have a look at item 2 and 3 -- items 2 and 3 of this order. In English this is page 2. What could be the reason for the president of the republic to decide in this way?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we can just scroll the document down so that I can see the date, please. All right. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The date is 20 April, 1994.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. This document has presented a kind of obstacle in the preparation of my report because I tried to fathom the reason and the authority for this document to be issued and the consequences of it. When I saw that it does not -- has any particular bearing on the subject of my report, I arrived at the following conclusion: It is obvious that in this period there were some disagreements, personal disagreements between the Commander-in-Chief and the commander of the VRS, and that the Commander-in-Chief had issued an order which was in contrary to his powers because it was well known that the commander of the VRS was appointed by the assembly and nobody can strip him of the rights stemming from the fact that he was the commander. Had the Commander-in-Chief acted properly, he would have probably initiated a procedure for dismissal of the commander of the VRS, and restore order. I was particularly perplexed by the fact that the Commander-in-Chief has sent an order to the corps which means that in a certain way he has ordered them not to carry out orders of their superior officer in certain situations. Based on further analysis, and specifically the analysis of the combat readiness in 1995 or other documents, it seems that either this agreement has been resolved completely, but there are some indications that it persisted in a certain form.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When the Main Staff received the Directive 7 signed, what were these tasks? Technically speaking, what did the Main Staff have to do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First you will notice an anomaly that at the beginning of Directive 7, there is no mention of it being addressed to the Main Staff because it says that it is addressed to the corps and the centre of military schools. From this specific example, we see that it was after all sent to the Main Staff, although it's not mentioned. The Main Staff initially acted as it had to. It forwarded the directive to the units according to the decision of the commander of -- in chief. And by doing so, that is what he did at the moment, and later on he took some further steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We know that the Main Staff created Directive 7/1. Did the Main Staff have the obligation to draft this directive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle if the Commander-in-Chief had prepared Directive 7 and forwarded it to a lower ranking unit, and it does not contain any military problems, that is to say, it satisfies all the standards applicable in military documents, then there is no need for the operationalisation of this directive. It is only followed through as if it had been issued by the Main Staff. The best example of that is Directive number 6 which was done in that manner. The fact that we have Directive 7/1 is a direct consequence of the fact that the Directive 7 was not clear enough and not useable enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document 5D361. This is Directive 7/1. Could page 2 be displayed on the screen, both for B/C/S and English, please. I would also wish to be allowed to give a hard copy of this directive to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please have a look at the text, in particular for task or item 2, tasks for the Army of the Republika Srpska. One can see that there is reference made to Directive 7. Could you tell us whether the task which I indicated in Directive 7/1 do correspond to those which are already indicated in Directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that task number 2 stems from the task issued by the superior command, that it's been taken over. And bearing in mind that this is a specific case, one can see that the commander of the VRS has decided to include tasks from Directive 7 in his directive and to elaborate it. This is completely consistent with what had been agreed and done before.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you look at item 3, paragraph number 3. In this paragraph, do you find the tasks of the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3 is not a task. The task is listed under item number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This item 3, what is its meaning in the directive? Could you tell us what this item 3 actually means here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what one can see from other directives, practically it describes the developments relating to the cessation of hostilities and the developments in Republika Srpska, and it provides some details for further operationalisation. One can say that neighbours are mentioned under item 3, and one can conditionally say that this is what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown, you see this in the English text on the next page, and in B/C/S it is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the one-but-last paragraph, there is mention of the fear of the elimination of the enclaves, the fear which the foreign powers have. Militarily speaking, does this part be linked -- can it be linked with the tasks entrusted to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that these statements referring to the characteristics of the execution of combat activities, movements of UNPROFOR, and the zones are in harmony with the structure of the directive, that is that they are found in point 3. And everything that relates to the tasks can be pulled out of whatever is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Please look at item 4, which is on page 3. In this item 4 where you have the decision, first of all, could you tell us who determined the content of this item 4? Who was in a position, who had the authority to determine this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the inviolable competence of the commander, and it is for the commander to make a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This decision from Directive 7/1, does it tell you with the decision and Directive 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision from Directive 7/1 must be in harmony with the task. And it is in harmony with the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the bottom of the page. In English it is page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In the last paragraph on this page, you can read that in the execution of the Sadejstvo operation, the other forces of the Army of the Republika Srpska cooperate to the objective, the goal, and this has to conform with Directive number 7 and this concerns the enclaves of Srebrenica, Zepa, Gorazde, and Bihac. According to your analysis, does this paragraph include to prepare possible conditions for the population? Unbearable conditions?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will now use a word that is frequently heard here, this conclusion from the military viewpoint is a matter of speculation. This is very precisely defined here what the Army of Republika Srpska should do with a view to successfully carrying out Operation Sadejstvo 95 and carrying out the task. It's elementary knowledge that when you want to carry out an operation, in one part of a war theatre, you are intensifying combat in all other parts to prevent the enemy from bringing his forces to the place which is the focus of your military activity. This is a typical example of action against enemy units in order to tie them down, and thus make it possible for the task to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could page 5 be displayed now, page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Item 5.3 you can see a task for the Drina Corps, which is described there. Is this task indicated in 5.3 tallies with item 4 of this directive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, the task of the Drina Corps is in line with the commander's decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And this task, does it tally with the tasks entrusted to the Drina Corps in Directive number 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently this task given to the Drina Corps in Directive number 7 was the reason or a major reason for Directive 7/1 to be drawn from it and to give this task. This is a task which in comparison with Directive number 7 is in military terms appropriate in terms of what a military unit can do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This task entrusted to the Drina Corps, does it include part of the task given in Directive number 7 concerning the creation of unbearable conditions for the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. You can see that the task is in line with the actual situation and with the decision of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to come back to page 2 of the directive. It's page 2 in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In item 2, last paragraph, last sentence of item 2, the Main Staff was to commence immediately plans and prepare for the execution of the Sadejstvo operation. When such a task has been entrusted, what are the organs of the Main Staff who had to take part in these activities, plans, and preparations?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's precisely stated here, and that's how it's done, the whole Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska is being included, and it begins to plan and carrying out organised preparations for the implementation of the strategical operation. This is a sufficient task for all the organisational units of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. From the on the left-hand side of yesterday's diagram, the staff to on the right-hand side the Administration for Planning, so that everyone has to begin preparations for this within their own sphere of competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: What is the role of the Administration in Charge of Operational And Educational Matters in the plans and the preparing of a strategic operation, called the Operation Sadejstvo in this case?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this directive and this sentence, the Chief of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska was supposed to make his own decision as to what and how the staff of the Army of Republika Srpska would carry out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I don't know where the problem is, but the question was not properly transcribed so I will repeat it. What was the role of the Administration in Charge of Operational and Educational Matters in the preparation of Operation Sadejstvo?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First there was the task to act on the orders of the Chief of Staff. The Chief of Staff was supposed to provide the initial elements on the basis of which the Administration for Operations and Training would proceed to work further. It may be assumed that the task issued by the Chief of Staff includes drawing up a plan as to how to carry out the planning of Operation Sadejstvo on the basis of which he would consult the commander, and this would be adopted and it would be binding on the entire Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Which tasks did the Chief of Staff entrust -- or could he entrust or should he normally have entrusted in the planning of a strategic operation to the Chief of the Administration for Operations and Training?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first task entrusted to him would be to draw up a plan for the drawing up of the documents for the strategic operation, but he would also give him a large number of initial documents which are of importance for the plan. These would be the essential elements, when to begin, when to finish, whom to involve, what forces to include, and based on this he would draft the plan, and then based on this draft further work would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One can see both in the Directive 7 and in this directive that the Spreca operation which should also be at the operational level according to this directive. Does the Main Staff have a role to play in the planning and the preparation of the Spreca operation? Perhaps also could you have a look at page 4, in particular page 4 in B/C/S, and I think it may be page 5 in English. In B/C/S it's completely at the bottom of the page, the East Bosnia Corps.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From task 5.2 and 5.3, the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska, one can see how he planned for Spreca 95 to be organised and carried out. We can see that he put in charge the commander of the East Bosnia Corps, and we can see that he ordered the commander of the Drina Corps to be included in the operation according to the plans of the commander of the East Bosnian Corps, and this indicates that the command of the East Bosnian Corps was supposed to draw up a draft decision on the map. It was supposed to draft the order and all the necessary documents and deliver this to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. At that point in time, the task of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska was for the staff to receive these documents, that is the officer for operations and training to look them over and give them with his comments to the Chief of Staff, and all the other organs of the command were to look at these drafts from the viewpoint of their own competencies and then forward this over to the Chief of Staff, and he would then accept and approve the operation or reject it. I wish to mention here, under normal conditions, or rather, as wartime conditions are not normal, in conditions where there is sufficient time, often there is a possibility for the competent commander in charge of carrying out the operation to report to the commander what his proposal is in the presence of the other members of the staff. So both methods are equally valid.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just to have a clear transcript on this matter, here we have the corps commander who was in charge of the performance of the operation, and in such a situation and when the conditions allow, he reports to the commander. Can you say the commander of which unit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander who issued the order for the operation; that is, the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When Directive 7/1 was transmitted to the Drina Corps, what were the tasks which the Drina Corps had to perform, those of Directive 7 or those of Directive 7/1?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the army it is well known with great precision, when you get your last order everything else that preceded it which is contrary to the last order ceases to be valid. Here the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska was very precise. He gave him a precise order where he said that things in Directive 7 were no longer valid and which things in Directive 7 could still be considered valid.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown P107. This is an order for the combat activities and the activities of the Drina Corps. The date of the order is 2 July, 1995. And could page 2 in B/C/S and 3 in English be displayed. I would also like to give a hard copy to the witness, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In item 2, the Drina Corps refers to Directive 7 and Directive 7/1 of the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska. Could you look at this item and tell us whether the task indicated in this order tallies or is in agreement with the tasks entrusted to the Drina Corps in the directive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order for active combat activities marked Krivaja 95, this was the name given it by the command of the Drina Corps, is part of the tasks received by the Drina Corps with Directive 7/1, and what remained in force from Directive 7, bearing in mind that this is only part of the tasks and is not reflected in the engagement at Spreca and so on, what has been extracted here are the tasks which are in accordance with Directive 7/1. It refers to all these elements of active combat activities with free forces, tied down those forces in the depth of the area, and part of the tasks separate the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. This is a task which has been ongoing for two years. It's not based either in Directive 7 or 7/1, but was present in every order issued in the past two years, so in item -- or point 2, it's inappropriate, but it could have been realised in quite a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One can see that in this task, the Drina Corps received as an assignment to reduce Zepa and Srebrenica to the urban zone. Could you from a military point of view determine what it is meant by the shrinking or reducing to the urban zone?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a town somewhere and the boundaries of the town, then that would be a precise task. The fact that Zepa is not a town and that Srebrenica and Zepa do not have such boundaries, this is a very imprecise task.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And from a military point of view, was it possible to execute this under this form, in this form?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you don't know what the boundaries are, you cannot execute it. But as they knew what the boundaries of the enclaves were, those were the boundaries within which they were able to execute it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the last page of the document be displayed now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to what is said on this last page, this order should have or would have been transmitted to the Main Staff. According to the documents you had at your disposal and which you perused, did you find any trace or anything which may confirm that this order has been transmitted?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the rules regulating the behaviour of the commands regulating the combat documents, there was no need to deliver this to the Main Staff, there was no obligation unless they wanted something to be seen. I don't know what, but according to what I saw nowhere did I see that this document was received or analysed or that any action was taken pursuant to it in the Main Staff. I never saw anywhere that the Main Staff, or what was called the basic command post, was apprised of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: If this document had been transmitted to the Main Staff, would the staff have made his own documents which would then have been transmitted to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had it been sent to the Main Staff, I believe that the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska would have ordered a better order to be drawn up, and this one to be disregarded.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One last question on this particular topic for the time being. Directive number 7, does it have a link with Directive number 4?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This stems from the very two documents, but I'm afraid that it might be mistranslated. These are documents at different levels, and therefore they are incomparable. Directive number 7 was issued at the national level based on the decision of the Commander-in-Chief, and Directive 4 is a military document issued at the strategic level issued by the commander of the Army of Republika Srpska. However, despite these huge differences, there are -- it contains two general tasks that cannot be compared at all, but if we know what the purpose of the directive is and at what period it was issued and to which they were addressed, even then there can be no comparison. Any such comparison would be artificial and exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In your report, and this is on page 5 and 6 in B/C/S, 5 and 7 in English, you mention establishment of protected areas. What is the basic fundamental condition from a military standpoint for an area to be considered as a protected area at the time of a war?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item is crucial for good understanding of the report, and any serious work must establish at the beginning the subject matter of the analysis. Item 6 is specifically characteristic for this work and for the understanding of the analysis of all the remaining elements that are involved. It is impossible not to say for any conditions relating to a protected area that it is not important. From the military point of view when analysing the fulfillment of all other conditions, this is the primary concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please just repeat, now, from a military point of view what is the prime or first condition?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic or the initial condition is demilitarisation of the zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to the documents which you were able to analyse, was this condition met regarding the Srebrenica and Zepa areas?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the documents that I reviewed except for the report of the Secretariat of the Secretary-General of the UN, which in one part contains the phrase "could be considered demilitarised," although it sounds strange, there is no document that confirms that demilitarisation has been effected. On the contrary, all the documents are saying that in this very small area, there was an inordinately huge armed force, the 8th Operations Group, in that very small area present all the time which was then transformed into the 28th Division in order for it to be able to be engaged in the final operations carried out by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: From the fact that demilitarisation was not effective, I mean, how was it reflected on the existence of the protected areas from the point of view of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the point of view not only of the Army of Republika Srpska, but from the view point of every soldier - and that is the basic thing - the fact that there was no demilitarisation practically means that this was not a protected area. That was a place where enemy forces were deployed carrying out offensive combat operations, tying up and engaging huge troops on the part of the VRS, and which present danger to the army who is responsible for that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to show you Exhibit 5D708. This is the order from the Main Staff dated 18th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This order is about the cease-fire and the procedure around Srebrenica. This order was issued immediately after the first agreement was signed about the demilitarisation of Srebrenica. Now, if you refer to this first page of this order, can we show the witness a little further down. Can we scroll down on the page, please. What conclusions can you draw about the intentions of the Army of Republika Srpska about Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one analyses carefully this order, it becomes obvious that the VRS had anticipated for this to be a true protected and demilitarised zone. In accordance with that it issued very precise and strict orders and instructions, and I would like specifically to highlight two apparently non-military instructions; and that is to forbid manoeuvres and movement of forces, and the bringing in of fresh troops. So this order is on the path of the creation of a proper protected zone as it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to show you two orders which are quite short from the Main Staff at about the same period of time. The first one is 5D1023 and is dated 23rd April 23rd, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would only like to did you to look at this order, and then I'll show you the other very similar order.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may I now show you Exhibit 5D1024, which is the order from the Main Staff dated 3rd May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to these orders, what was the position of the Main Staff, particularly relating to the second order about two weeks after the signature of the first agreement on demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three orders represent the commitment of the VRS, that this is essentially a protected area. The first one was issued to their units instructing them how to behave themselves, and this one deals with the approval for the passage of units, aid, and doctors, and also UNPROFOR commander.
