All that is in compliance with the conditions for a protected zone, and that is to ensure a proper control being carried out by the UN forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now show you Exhibit P2742. This is also an order from the Main Staff from the 1st of May, 1993. This is the order for the liberation of Zepa and Gorazde. What I'm interested in in this order is at page 5 in B/C/S and page 8 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the paragraph starting, "In the second phase ..." and which talks about disarmament of the Muslim units. This formation talks about the disarmament of Muslim formations, and according to this paragraph, the idea was to make it possible for the civilian population to move to central Bosnia or to remain in town, provided that they recognised the Serbian rule. From a military point of view, does this paragraph include a number of irregularities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we take out of context this, then one can say that there is a certain irregularity and that is the disarming of the civilian population. However, if we put this order back into the context and look at all the forms of the war that was being waged and that very often enemy soldiers dressed as women or wore civilian clothes, then it's obvious that the process of disarming was intended to search everyone and find whether they had any weapons or not. On the other hand, this is a rather frequent sentence that appears because in this region fear was often instilled among the civilian population by the armies.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you please read the paragraph that I pointed to before, please.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole or just the latter part?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The whole paragraph, the one that starts by "in the second phase..."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the second phase which is to last 5 to 6 days, regroup the forces and from the circular axis bring fresh forces and continue fierce attack against Gorazde and take the dominant peaks around Gorazde and encircle it as soon as possible and completely. This way conditions are to be created for the disarming of the remaining Muslim formations, and it will make it possible for the civilian population to move to central Bosnia or to remain in town, provided they recognise the Serbian rule."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: My question was only about this paragraph. Now, does this paragraph entail a number of irregularities, militarily speaking?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, on this same page in the B/C/S version and also in the English version but that is further down on the page, one sees that this operation was supposed to be conducted by the Main Staff. And according to this paragraph, Colonel Ilic was in charge of forces engaged in the liberation of Gorazde, and while Colonel Miletic was in charge of forces engaged in the liberation of Zepa. First of all, I should like to ask you a question about Colonel Ilic. Do you know what the position of Colonel Ilic was in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Head of the Operations and Training Administration with the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, without this order, would Colonel Ilic have had the authorities required and indicated in this order for the operation in Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what if this order had not existed, what would have been the competencies and authorities of Colonel Ilic in this operation in Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His regular duties and responsibilities as the head of the operations and training administration stationed at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Colonel Ilic who was in charge of the forces in Gorazde, did he have in this specific operation authority over Colonel Miletic who was in charge of forces in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One can see clearly here how the Main Staff of the VRS had planned the execution of this operation. The Main Staff of the VRS was in charge of conducting the operation, Colonel Ilic was in charge of one part, that is Gorazde, and Colonel Miletic was in charge of the other part, i.e., Zepa. The two of them had powers according to their tasks and they were absolutely equal in performing their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, at the time of military activities around Srebrenica and Zepa in July 1995, did General Miletic have certain powers which he had during this operation in Zepa in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely none. His powers are precisely defined here, and that is to be in charge of these forces. In June and July he was at the command post discharging his duties, and particularly the aspect that I mentioned before relating to the VRS and that was the time when the commander was in the area which automatically reduces the duties of the head of the Operations and Training Administration head.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit 5D1201. This is Directive number 5 dated 25th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you tell us what were the military reasons for this directive to be drawn up in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a period, that is 1993 is particularly characteristic for developments in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was a time when all the three entities insisted on autonomy at the same time. The Croatian leadership was the loudest in insisting on the autonomy of their entity. That was also a period when these two entities started clashing with each other in a very prominent way.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 8 in English and page 4 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the task for the Drina Corps. At the very top of the page in English. In this directive, you can see that the Drina Corps had as a task to contain the Muslim forces which remained in Gorazde, Zepa, and Srebrenica during the whole siege and the encircling period. In light of the agreements on demilitarisation which date back to April and May 1993, how do you explain the existence of this task entrusted to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This task given to the Drina Corps was the result of the fact that the VRS had seen for itself and became quite certain that there was no militarisation of Gorazde, Srebrenica, and Zepa. Having realised that at that point there was no other option, it decided to hold and contain firmly the units deployed in the area and to prevent them linking up and engaging in coordinated actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... block off the Muslim forces, why is this word "completely," why is this word included in the directive? Sorry, my mistake, I'd like to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Either now or after the break, it's up to you. It's your choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have a break now, I still have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: We were talking about this task entrusted to the Drina Corps which was to block the forces, the Muslim forces, block them completely. Why was it necessary to block completely the Muslim forces, and why is this word "completely" necessary?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This completeness was the consequence of the stay in the enclave of large military forces which used every possible means to replenish themselves and which represented a latent threat to the Drina Corps and the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: About this task entrusted to the Drina Corps, from a military point of view, was this task imply moving the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no way. This can be seen from the order issued by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska where practically all action and all movements were halted and the protected area was accepted as a good thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 5 in B/C/S and page 10 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One can see at item 5 -- item 7 that the Main Staff orders or commands in the operation which is mentioned in this directive. Does a similar task -- was a similar task given to the Main Staff in Directive number 7 concerning the activities, the combat activities around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically in this document, in this directive, the item 7 formulated in this way is redundant. When the Main Staff issues an order, it doesn't forward the order. The only thing that can be concluded is that the Main Staff will be in charge, the directive specifies who is to do what and the planned operations were conducted in line with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what was the role of the Main Staff in the actions entrusted to the Drina Corps concerning -- concerning Srebrenica in the case of Directive 7?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards Srebrenica, in the context of Directive number 7, there was only one possible potential task which was established and which could take place, and the operation would be planned and led by the Main Staff, which would be in charge of it. If you analysed the document in detail, you were able to see that Operation Jadar did not have a number, so it was not actually carried out, it was only planned, if that's the one you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: No, not specifically. I asked whether Directive number 7 gave the authority to the Main Staff for this order to command for the combat activities which had to be ordained around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1203.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the order of the 7th July, 1995 which is linked to the realisation of the order. It was 1993, 1993. You can see that this document is addressed to the Drina Corps, and one also can see on page -- at the bottom page 1 in English, one can also see that the specific tasks were entrusted to units of the Drina Corps. Why does the commander of the staff determine precisely the tasks of the units of the Drina Corps? The commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see here that the tasks set by the commander very clearly and precisely to the units of the Drina Corps have as their purpose making it possible for the Sarajevo Romanija and the East Bosnian Corps carrying out the tasks and operation they have been assigned. This a textbook example of a commander ordering actions to distract the enemy and make it possible for the other actions to be carried out more efficiently.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D963 which is Directive number 6. This is a directive from the Supreme Command dated 11 November, 1993. Could page 5 in B/C/S and in English be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One can see on this page what are the tasks of the Drina Corps, and one can see that the task was to besiege the enemy forces to inflict constantly losses to these forces and to interrupt or hinder their communications. Obstruct their communications. Could you explain from a military point of view why this task comprised to inflict to the enemy constantly some losses?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this task to be understood, why was it persistently reiterated, it would be a good thing to show the tasks given to the 28th Division from the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993 as soon as these enclaves were established. At that time the tasks were as follows: That active combat should constantly be undertaken to inflict losses on the enemy and tie down enemy forces. And this is the order on the other side, to prevent forces from Srebrenica and Zepa spilling over to the 2nd Corps and other forces, and thus preventing them from taking action.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did this task from a military point of view also include irregularities?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's very precise. It says block enemy forces, inflict constant losses, and prevent communication, so it is very precise in military terms and it refers to enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 3 of this directive, and it's also page 3 for the English text. Just at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Item 3 defines a task of the Army of the Republika Srpska and one may read, inter alia, that this task speaks about the achievement of objective conditions to reach the strategic objectives of the Army of the Republika Srpska during this war. So here you have two tasks concerning Sarajevo first, and the Neretva river. Would it be possible now to go to page 4 in B/C/S. Then here you have the two other tasks concerning river Una, and widening of the borders in the north-east area. Was one of these tasks about the Drina river? Sorry, did one of these goals have to do with the Drina river?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's important that you separated the task from the goal. The task was given previously and the goal was announced, and none of this has anything to do with the Drina river.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you give an explanation why among these four goals, strategic goals for the army, there is no third strategic goal which we had seen on Monday concerning the valley of the Drina river?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we are trying to make a connection between two different documents, the state goals and the military goals. One thing is important, a military goal can never be greater than a state goal. It can never involve more. And every military goal which is within the scope of a state goal is defined in this way. Why do they differ? Well, quite simply probably at that time there was no need for the goal stated here to exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document 5D954 [as interpreted]. This is an order modifying the directive. It amends the directive. So I asked for 964.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Now, this is an order from President Karadzic, modifying Directive number 6 of the 12th of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the bottom of the page 1 be shown in English, and also the case in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Here you have the task of the Republika Srpska's army described, and according to the tasks which are indicated here in this item 2, were the goals, the strategic goals as defined in Directive number 6, were they in any way modified, changed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The strategic goals included in Directive number 6 are goals and they remain goals. We can establish a link between the task from Directive 6, and this addition to the -- or rather, correction, modification of the decision issued by the Commander-in-Chief. You can see from this that he focused on three tasks which narrow down the activity envisaged in Directive number 6, and make it possible for the tasks to be carried out more efficiently. The military goals from Directive number 6 cannot be linked to these tasks. Goals are goals and until they are transformed into tasks they remain merely goals.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown page 3 from the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The second paragraph in B/C/S and third paragraph in English. In this paragraph the Drina Corps has to be reinforced with a reserve from the Supreme Command. Do you have any idea of what is this reserve of the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the problem I mentioned. I find it strange that a reconstruction of the organisational plan of both the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were drawn up to see what forces were included. According to the documents I saw, it was practically one regiment and one sabotage battalion. I think those were all the reserves that they had under their command.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the Supreme Command or the President Radovan Karadzic have his own forces as a president?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Supreme Command had no forces. The Commander-in-Chief had only the Army of Republika Srpska. Those were the only military forces he had. There were no other military units or institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown document 5D1033.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order from the Main Staff dated 26 April, 1994. This order speaks about preventing communications between the Muslims on the Kladanj and Zepa axis. I don't want to harp on it, but I'm interested especially in item 1 of this order. Which indicates that the artillery support, the action has to be executed without support from artillery. Without any artillery support. What was the military reason for such an order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To give an answer to this, one must be familiar with the situation, but we do have sufficient elements to provide a highly probable reply, and that is that the Main Staff of the VRS evaluated that the task should be carried out and could be carried out in this way in order to save artillery ammunition needed for other activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 5D1223.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the plan of the Drina Corps to eliminate and to realise the tasks on the 10th of July, 1994. Does the making of such plans -- was it usual, is it usual in an army to make such plans?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said when we were speaking about the analysis, after every inspection, every visit, every analysis, every briefing, and one can see here that there has been a briefing, when the commander's report what the essential problems are, and the command underlines what it has observed, a plan always has to be drawn up to remove any weaknesses and shortcomings. This sort of activity is obligatory.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 2 in B/C/S and 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just to avoid any repetition, could you simply tell us whether these plans are made -- the elimination plan is elaborated on the same system as a monthly or annual work plain, or are they elaborated according to another methodology?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These plans are developed according to the elements of combat readiness. This plan is also defined according to the elements of combat readiness. Analysis of work-plans are done quite differently and corrected quite differently. This was pursuant to a briefing according to the elements of combat readiness and the first such element is command and control.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And what is the organ of the command which is in charge of drawing up plans of this nature?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff is in charge of this, and it is carried out by the assistant of the Chief of Staff for operations and training, and all those involved in implementing the plan, every organ of the command, makes proposals as to activities, those in charge, and so on and so forth, and the operative then incorporates that into the plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to show you page 3 in B/C/S, which is page 5 and 6 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please look at point 5.1. According to this point 1, the regular reports for regular combats must be transferred in time and must have quality content. Can you explain why the quality of the reports matters?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analysing the large number of cases of the delivery of combat reports in the JNA, the VRS and other armed forces, this is a typical problem. Combat reports are often a burden on the commander, they have to submit this at a particular time, collect all the elements, and then send this at a defined time. Often units use a cliche, they fail to include important things that happened, and they send an incomplete combat report, and then the command is not well informed. And then as a consequence interim reports are sent, or the actual situation in the unit does not correspond to what is in the report. That's why it's stated here that these reports have to be done on time and that they have to be done well and not just according to the cliche.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to show you P2749.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is the order from the Main Staff dated 22nd of July, 1994. Looking at the preamble of the order, you can see that it follows a briefing, which was held on the 1st of July, 1994, and that it was pursuant to the report from the commander of the Drina Corps to the commander of the Main Staff. According to point number 1 in this order, the order of the Main Staff from 18th of April, 1993, is the order which followed immediately after the disarmament agreement is declared null and void. What were the possible reasons why this order from the 18th of April, 1993 was made null and void? And I would like you to give us a very brief answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, what is characteristic of this document, it is realistic to assume that the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS was with the Drina Corps at the time, and that the briefing of the commander was organised there. Because commanders of regiments and brigades were present there and they indicated and addressed the problems they are facing in their respective zones. We see that Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde enclaves were mentioned. Most probably one can deduce that in view of the huge combat operations launched from these enclaves that both the army and the population were suffering losses. And in order to carry out good control and blockade, this order had to be annulled because if you remember this order banned any movement of the units of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you now please refer to points 2 and 3 of this order. Now, looking at these two points, are they in disagreement with the agreement on demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not contrary to the agreement on demilitarisation but since the demilitarisation was not carried out, this obligation was in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 2 in the English version, please, which is also page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please focus on item or point 5 and tell us whether point 5 is contrary to the agreement on demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. It is even in conformity with the agreement because it enables unhindered movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have Exhibit 5D1176.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is an order from the president of the republic dated 1st of August, 1994, which is sent to the Ministry of Interior. As you can see, this order is much shorter, but it more or less addresses the same orders as the Main Staff -- that of the Main Staff, particularly the order of the 22nd of July. Why did the president of the republic give to the Ministry of the Interior practically at the same time the same task as the one that was entrusted to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska and the police constitute a single armed force. The president of the republic is now giving a task to the forces of the Ministry of the Interior within their purview and in cooperation with the army based on specific plans to resolve this problem. If you analyse the document, which is not what I did when it concerns MUP, one can nevertheless see that all the conditions here are in place for a coordinated action to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now show you 5D1224. This is an order from the Drina Corps dated 6 of September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This order refers to the order from the Main Staff from 5th of September, 1994, and as you can see, this is still to prevent communications between the enclaves and between the enclaves at Kladanj and Tuzla. In light of the fact that there was an order from the staff from April 1994, and as we've just seen there was the order from the 22nd of July, 1994, why was it necessary to issue another in order in September 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfulfilled previous order require a new order to be issued in order to correct the situation and for it to be implemented. It is obvious that since this order was issued a couple of days after the previous ones, in the meantime, the Main Staff also issued an order for the 8th Operations Group who at the time was in Srebrenica, was creating huge problems for the VRS and they were looking for every possible way to resolve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now show you Exhibit 5D1034. This is the report from the Drina Corps which followed the order from the Main Staff from September 5th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: From this type of report, which is not a usual combat report, neither is it an interim report. Was that sort of report a usual one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When an order is received, it's usually defines when and what kind of reports are to be submitted, either the regular combat reports or other. Once you receive an order and start implementing it, it is customary for the commander of the unit to brief his superior commander about the implementation of the order. This is done often through communications line or in writing as was the case here. The commander of the Drina Corps is informing him of how the tasks were being carried out in compliance with the order received on the 5th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just before the break, I'd like to show you 5D1040.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This again is an order stemming from the Drina Corps about communications between the enclaves. Now, what I'm interested in is right at the top, at the very top of the document, because if you look at the preamble of this document, it is -- it seems that the forces in the Srebrenica enclave, the enemy forces, were preparing for an offensive operation, and were getting prepared for that. You have already said that there were military forces present in the enclaves. How is it possible for these forces to be manned well enough and to have enough strength in order to conduct an offensive?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN KOSOVAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, when you say enough strength, it might be misleading. One immediately thinks about a group of soldiers. There was an operations group in Srebrenica which is a formation that exceeds the capacity of the region in all its aspect, and their task was to regroup. All the documents that are available and that I've seen show that these forces were supplied with weapons and ammunition from the air by land and even through humanitarian aid. They were exceptionally supplied with the appropriate ammunition because the focus of the supply was on the infantry ammunition, and it is a decisive factor when it comes to operations carried out in this region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can stop here for today. Thank you Ms. Fauveau, thank you gentlemen -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, just for the benefit of my colleagues, I think that I will be able to finish during today's session, probably towards the end of the session, but I think I'll be able to finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. Tomorrow, not today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, more or less those of you who had indicated a significant amount of time for cross-examination - I can recall one instance of at least three hours, for example - will please let us know in the morning or let the Prosecution know if you still are sticking to that amount, so that the Prosecution will know whether they will start tomorrow or next week. We will reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. Same advisory as before, please do not discuss the subject matter with anyone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of January, 2009 at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
